column1: # muster route partition manifest — WHICH SIDE EACH UPSTREAM ROUTE LANDS ON.
# 🔴 THIS FILE IS A MIGRATION-TIME ARTIFACT AND IS MEANT TO BE DELETED.
# DELETE-BY CONDITION, stated so this cannot become an object nobody can close:
#   routes_golden_test.go with it, in the SAME pull request — when the code
#   carve is finished and reconciled. The mechanical check that closes it:
#     1. both projects' `routes.golden` have been regenerated against their
#     2. every `muster` row below appears in muster's golden and not in the
#        other project's; every `router` row appears in the other project's
#        golden and not in muster's; every `shared` row appears in BOTH; and
#     3. any row deliberately dropped instead of moved is named in that pull
#   WHO CHECKS IT: the reviewer of that pull request, reading the two golden
#   diffs against this file. It is a diff, not a judgement call — if the three
#   conditions above hold, this file has no remaining reader and goes.
#   In the same pull request, flip `routePhase` in routes_golden_test.go from
#   `carving` to `carved`, which is what arms the route floor.
#   UNTIL THEN: this is the ONLY machine-readable record of which side a route
#   was meant to land on. The plan document it was derived from does not
#   enumerate its own partition — it states bucket totals and nothing else,
#   which is precisely why this file exists.
# FORMAT: three TAB-separated fields per row, sorted by route (byte order).
#     router   — stays with the permission router, i.e. the project muster is
#                being extracted from. (Spelled `router` rather than by name:
#                this repository's leak gate refuses the upstream project's
#                real name, deliberately, and that gate is not to be edited.)
#     shared   — the UI shell / infra surface BOTH projects need. Shared rows
#                are DUPLICATED, not moved: they end up in both goldens.
#   upstream-registrar is the file and registration function that owns the
#   route upstream. It is derived, not typed: every row was produced by parsing
#   the upstream package's non-test sources for literal patterns handed to
#   Handle/HandleFunc, then joined to the upstream golden. All 162 golden
#   routes resolved to exactly one registrar; none was left unmatched.
#   Upstream golden at commit a3dfea065, read 2026-09: 162 routes
#   the upstream test's own parser applies: comment and blank lines dropped).
#   🔴 THE PLAN DOCUMENT SAYS 174, AND 174 IS STALE BY EXACTLY TWELVE ROUTES.
#   The commit above retired an entire authorisation tier and deleted its
#   twelve `/operator` patterns; 174 is the count at its PARENT commit. Both
#   numbers were re-derived here rather than copied:
#       parent of a3dfea065 : 174 routes, 12 of them `/operator`
#   The plan states "90 -> muster, 82 -> the other side, plus the 2 chief
#   terminal routes, plus 14 shared". 90 + 82 + 2 = 174 = its own total, which
#   leaves the 14 unaccounted for UNLESS they are already inside one of the two
#   numbers. They are: the plan's own floor paragraph says muster lands at
#   "~90 (~104 with duplicated shell routes)", and 90 + 14 = 104. So the 14 sit
#   inside the 82, and the only self-consistent reading is:
#        2  chief terminal routes (a third bucket, in neither)
#      174  total, each route counted exactly once
#   This file uses the other, non-overlapping convention — shared is its own
#   bucket — so its three counts also sum to the total, and muster's projected
#   registration count is muster + shared, not muster alone.
# THIS FILE'S OWN COUNTS (re-derived, not copied from the plan)
#   ⚠ 70 / 147 / 84 UNTIL THE CARDS LOST THEIR PREVIEW. GET
#   /ui/agents/{id}/recent served only the cards' lazy recent-log slot and was
#   deleted with it (operator decision: no previews on cards).
#   ⚠ 67 / 66 / 81 UNTIL muster GREW ITS OWN WEB PUSH. The three /api/push/*
#   rows moved router → muster then: muster holds its own VAPID key and
#   subscription table (migration 0013), so those three routes are served
#   here and no longer by the router. That is a deliberate re-cut of the line
#   below ("stays: … push"), not a carve-time drift.
#   ⚠ THESE WERE 82 / 162 / 96 AT THE CARVE. The 15 privilege and runbook rows
#   were deleted when those subsystems were removed (muster PR #49), so the
#   manifest no longer lists routes that exist on neither side. The plan
#   comparison below is about the carve-time counts and is left as written.
#   🔴 THIS PARTITION DISAGREES WITH THE PLAN'S, AND THE DISAGREEMENT CANNOT BE
#   RECONCILED FROM THE PLAN. Normalised onto the plan's 174-route base by
#   adding back the twelve `/operator` routes (the retired tier was agent and
#   board machinery, so they belong on muster's side), this file gives
#   muster 82+12=94 where the plan gives 90, and a staying side of
#   66+14=80 where the plan gives 82+2=84 — a four-route gap each way. It
#   cannot be attributed, because the plan never enumerates which routes it put
#   where, only totals. The rows below are derived from the live route table
#   and the plan's stated cut line; where they differ from the plan's totals,
#   the rows win, and the totals are the thing that was never checked.
# THE CUT LINE THIS PARTITION APPLIES (from the plan's decision table)
#   moves : tasks, dispatch/agents, chief, runbooks, privilege
#   stays : permission routing, push, sse, autoapprove, suggest, attention,
#           tmux, termwrite, layout, transcript, recap, archive
#   Mechanically: every route whose upstream registrar is one of
#   registerGitHubRoutes is `muster`; plus the three chief routes and the three
#   tab-shell pages (/tasks, /agents, /repos) the moving tabs serve. The 14
#   shell/infra routes are `shared`. Everything else is `router`.
# ⚠ ONE DERIVED CLAIM IN THE PLAN DID NOT SURVIVE. It says "four of eight tabs
# move". The route table has eight tab shells — requests, tasks, attention,
# repos, agents, suggestions, tmux, layout — and the cut line moves THREE of
# them (tasks, repos, agents). No fourth tab is on the moving side. Either the
# plan counted something that is not a tab, or the number is wrong. Nothing
# below depends on it, but do not build on it.
# NOTE (GET /agent/muster): RENAMED IN THE MOVE. Upstream spells this with the upstream CLI's binary
# name, which this repository's leak gate refuses to spell and which muster's
# own CLI replaces anyway. The muster-side spelling is the one the step-17
# diff compares; the upstream-side row will not match textually.
# NOTE (GET /api/projects): The task-create directory picker. Its upstream store reads the permission
# router's own table, which the source plan measured EMPTY in production —
# so this route moves, but its data source does not come with it. Expect to
# either drop the picker or repoint it at a muster-local source.
# NOTE (GET /health): SHARED means DUPLICATED, NOT MOVED: both projects register their own copy.
# All 14 shared rows are therefore expected to appear in BOTH goldens after
# NOTE (GET /repos): LEAST CERTAIN BLOCK (5 rows: this, GET /ui/repos, GET /github/connect,
# GET /github/callback, POST /github/disconnect). Assigned to muster because
# the repo list exists to pick a repo when DISPATCHING an agent — the agent
# registrar already owns GET /ui/agents/repos. The source plan never
# enumerates its own partition, so this assignment is derived here, not
# inherited. If the Repos tab turns out to serve anything on the staying
# side, these five move back and the counts below shift by 5.
# NOTE (POST /api/term/chief/new-session): 🔴 THE SOURCE PLAN CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON THESE TWO ROWS. Its seam table says
# the chief-specific terminal routes are DELETED (muster drives the generic
# /api/term/* pair with an asserted actor instead); its CLI section and its
# route-partition paragraph both say they STAY. Recorded as `router` because
# NEITHER reading moves them here — but whoever runs step 17 must settle
# delete-vs-stay rather than inherit this row as agreement.
# NOTE (POST /api/term/chief/send-keys): See the note on POST /api/term/chief/new-session — same unresolved pair.
# NOTE (POST /chief/provision): The one handler that moves out of a file that otherwise stays: the chief
